what: Counts of the Sherlock Holmes corpus and of the remakes corpus (v2/second/PLAN.md, Sections 2, 3, 10 and 15), each computed from a committed file by v2/second/corpus_counts.py. value: the count; what: what it counts; source: the file and how it was counted.

texts.what: texts in the corpus (the plot section of each work's own Wikipedia article)

texts_by_kind.what: texts by kind: the Conan Doyle stories, the screen works, the ancestors (read, used by no test), the detective films (the negatives of E1) and the pages kept in the file but not used

sentences.what: sentences in all the texts together
sentences.source: data/second/holmes/corpus.jsonl: sum of the lengths of `sentences`

sentences_per_text.what: sentences per text (PLAN Section 2 sets the fewest a text may have and the most that are kept)

name_free_texts.what: name-free versions of the texts (every name replaced by a code)

screen_works_by_medium.what: screen works by medium, from the kind of the page's first infobox
screen_works_by_medium.source: data/second/holmes/corpus.jsonl: `medium` of the rows whose `group` is screen

screen_works_by_the_readers_label.what: screen works by the label the readers of the articles gave (series: the page is about a whole series, not one work)

pages_about_a_whole_series.what: screen-work pages that, by the readers' label, are about a whole series; they stay in the corpus
pages_about_a_whole_series.source: data/second/holmes/works.json: works whose kind is series

novels.source: data/second/holmes/spec.json: strata, over the ids of `early`

short_stories.source: data/second/holmes/spec.json: strata, over the ids of `early`

primary_adaptations.what: screen works whose article states at least one story at tier A (an adaptation) or B (a loose or partial adaptation)

stories_with_a_primary_adaptation.what: stories that at least one primary adaptation names at tier A or B

primary_adaptations_naming_more_than_one.what: primary adaptations that name two or more stories at tier A or B
primary_adaptations_naming_more_than_one.source: data/second/holmes/spec.json: adaptations (values with more than one story)

primary_adaptations_of_the_hound_of_the_.what: primary adaptations that are versions of The Hound of the Baskervilles
primary_adaptations_of_the_hound_of_the_.source: data/second/holmes/spec.json: adaptations whose stories include id 2 (the row of corpus.jsonl titled The Hound of the Baskervilles)

straight_adaptations.what: screen works with a tier A story (the article states it is an adaptation of the story)

straight_adaptations_of_the_hound_of_the.what: straight adaptations that are versions of The Hound of the Baskervilles
straight_adaptations_of_the_hound_of_the.source: data/second/holmes/spec.json: adaptations_straight whose stories include id 2

elements_only_works.what: screen works whose article states only that elements, characters or a title are taken (tier C and nothing stronger)

stories_named_by_the_elements_only_works.what: stories the elements-only works name at tier C

screen_works_with_no_stated_source.what: screen works whose article states no Conan Doyle source (the baseline of E2 and the later works of E3)

works_the_two_readers_disagreed_on.what: screen works on which the two readers of the articles differed; a third reader read them and the majority decided

screen_works_in_which_holmes_appears.what: screen works in which, by both readers, Sherlock Holmes appears as a character

screen_works_by_era.what: the screen works (the franchise of E1) by era
screen_works_by_era.source: data/second/holmes/spec.json: era, over the ids of `franchise`

detective_films_by_era.what: the detective films (the negatives of E1) by era
detective_films_by_era.source: data/second/holmes/spec.json: era, over the ids of `negatives`

lineage_works.what: works of the lineage of E2: the stories and the screen works

later_works_widened.what: screen works that are not primary adaptations (the wider set of later works that E3 reports beside)

screen_works_that_are_films.what: screen works that are films (the franchise narrowed to its films, a robustness check of E1)

texts_that_are_documents_of_v2_reference.what: films of the Holmes corpus (screen works and detective films) that are, in an older wording, among the film plots of v2's reference corpus

of_which_background_plots.what: of those, the ones among its background plots (they are left out of the base rates)
of_which_background_plots.source: data/second/holmes/spec.json: in_reference_corpus whose set is bgplot

of_which_other_reference_plots.what: of those, the ones among its other film plots
of_which_other_reference_plots.source: data/second/holmes/spec.json: in_reference_corpus whose set is not bgplot

reference_documents_by_kind_of_text.what: the same films by kind of text
reference_documents_by_kind_of_text.source: data/second/holmes/spec.json: in_reference_corpus > id, with `group` of corpus.jsonl

texts_shared_with_the_batman_study.what: texts that are, sentence for sentence, texts of the Batman study (PLAN Section 4 names them)

stories_with_page_views.what: stories with a page-view total (the popularity measure of E3)
stories_with_page_views.source: data/second/holmes/pageviews.json: keys that are ids of spec.json `early`

months_of_page_views.what: months in the page-view window of each story

texts_asked_question_h1.what: texts each model was asked question H1 about (which famous hero is the story about?)

texts_asked_question_h2.what: texts each model was asked question H2 about (which Conan Doyle story does it tell or adapt?): the lineage works

background_plots_of_the_base_rates.what: background film plots the base rates are counted over (v2's background plots less those left out)

share_of_name_free_sentences_matching_th.what: share of name-free sentences that match the iconography list (they are dropped in one clause of E1), in screen works and in detective films

words_of_an_article_shown_to_the_readers.what: the most words of a screen work's article that the readers were shown (plot, cast and end sections left out)
words_of_an_article_shown_to_the_readers.source: v2/second/build_holmes.py: the default of max_words in article_without_plot

articles_cut_short_by_the_word_limit.what: screen-work articles that were cut short for the readers: the text shown is exactly as long as the limit (a longer text is never shown)
articles_cut_short_by_the_word_limit.source: results/v2/second/readers/holmes_sources/r1_*.prompt.txt: articles whose section text has as many words as the limit

screen_works_from_2000_by_medium.what: the screen works from 2000 on by medium, from the kind of the page's first infobox (the era in which most screen works are not films)
screen_works_from_2000_by_medium.source: data/second/holmes/corpus.jsonl: `medium` of the screen works whose `era` is from_2000

screen_works_from_2000_that_are_not_film.what: screen works from 2000 on that are not films: episodes, video games and television films or programmes
screen_works_from_2000_that_are_not_film.source: data/second/holmes/corpus.jsonl: screen works whose `era` is from_2000 and whose `medium` is not film

film_table_rows.what: rows of the film table (the pinned copy of the Wikipedia Movie Plots table)

film_table_pages.what: Wikipedia pages of the film table

film_table_pages_with_several_rows.what: pages the table lists in several rows (one row per page is used)

film_table_pages_where_a_later_row_is_us.what: of those, the pages for which a row other than the first is used

sentences_with_remake_remade_or_reboot.what: sentences in the opening of a film's article that contain remake, remade or reboot

statements_read.what: statements: those sentences that link to at least one other page of the table; each was read by two readers

statements_the_two_readers_read_differen.what: statements the two readers read differently; a third reader read them

stated_pairs.what: pairs (remake, source) stated by at least one statement and contradicted by none

kept_pairs.what: stated pairs that meet every condition of PLAN Section 3 (years in order, both plots long enough, two different texts)

dropped_pairs.what: stated pairs that fail a condition

dropped_pairs_by_reason.what: the dropped pairs by the condition they fail

kept_pairs_by_block_and_wording.what: kept pairs by block (the industries of the two films) and by the wording of the statement (firm or loose)

kept_pairs_by_wording.what: kept pairs by the wording of the statement

copied_pairs.what: kept pairs flagged copied: at least 10% of the five-word sequences of the remake's text are also in the source's text

set_primary.what: the primary set (firm Indian cross-industry pairs): pairs, how many are copied and not copied, how many share under 1% of five-word sequences, and their distinct remakes, sources and families
set_primary.source: data/second/remakes/pairs.json: pairs > * > wording, block, copied, share_of_five_word_sequences_also_in_source, remake, source, family

set_firm_other_cross_industry.what: the firm pairs of other cross-industry remakes: pairs, how many are copied and not copied, how many share under 1% of five-word sequences, and their distinct remakes, sources and families
set_firm_other_cross_industry.source: data/second/remakes/pairs.json: pairs > * > wording, block, copied, share_of_five_word_sequences_also_in_source, remake, source, family

set_firm_same_industry.what: the firm pairs within one industry: pairs, how many are copied and not copied, how many share under 1% of five-word sequences, and their distinct remakes, sources and families
set_firm_same_industry.source: data/second/remakes/pairs.json: pairs > * > wording, block, copied, share_of_five_word_sequences_also_in_source, remake, source, family

set_firm_all.what: all the firm pairs: pairs, how many are copied and not copied, how many share under 1% of five-word sequences, and their distinct remakes, sources and families
set_firm_all.source: data/second/remakes/pairs.json: pairs > * > wording, block, copied, share_of_five_word_sequences_also_in_source, remake, source, family

set_loose_all.what: the loose pairs: pairs, how many are copied and not copied, how many share under 1% of five-word sequences, and their distinct remakes, sources and families
set_loose_all.source: data/second/remakes/pairs.json: pairs > * > wording, block, copied, share_of_five_word_sequences_also_in_source, remake, source, family

primary_pairs.what: pairs of the primary set: firm statements, both films from different Indian industries
primary_pairs.source: data/second/remakes/pairs.json: pairs with wording firm and block indian_cross_industry

primary_pairs_copied.what: primary pairs flagged copied (the positive control of the heredity test)

primary_pairs_not_copied.what: primary pairs not flagged copied (the confirmatory heredity test is run on these)

primary_pairs_with_under_1pct_of_five_wo.what: primary pairs whose remake shares under 1% of its five-word sequences with the source

primary_remakes.what: distinct remakes in the primary set

primary_sources.what: distinct sources in the primary set

primary_families.what: families in the primary set (a family is one cluster in every test)

primary_remakes_with_two_or_more_documen.what: remakes of the primary set with two or more documented sources (each pair is one entry)

families.what: families of films in all (films joined by a remake statement, a shared article, or copied text); every kept pair lies within one family

relatives_in_no_kept_pair.what: films read that belong to the family of a kept pair but are in no kept pair themselves (never a candidate for their family's remakes)

films_of_the_kept_pairs.what: distinct films in the kept pairs

remakes_of_the_kept_pairs.what: distinct remakes in the kept pairs (the rows of the counts)

sources_of_the_kept_pairs.what: distinct sources in the kept pairs

films_read.what: films read: every film of the table with a long enough cleaned plot from an industry that is the source's in some kept pair, and every film of a kept pair

films_read_by_industry.what: films read by the table's industry label

films_read_of_the_indian_industries.what: films read whose industry is one of the Indian industries
films_read_of_the_indian_industries.source: data/second/remakes/films_index.json: films > * > origin, with the list INDIAN of v2/second/build_remakes.py

sentences_per_film.what: cleaned sentences per film read (PLAN Section 3 sets the fewest a film may have and the most that are kept)

films_read_by_each_model.what: films each model read (Llama 3.3 70B read the films of the Indian industries and every film of a pair)

models_that_read_every_film.source: results/v2/second/remakes_verify_<tag>.json: films_read_by_the_model equal to the films of films_index.json

cells_recounted_per_model.what: counts of shared units (each remake against each film of a pair) recounted away from the GPU machine for each model; none differs

candidates_per_primary_pair.what: candidate films per primary pair, the source not counted: films of the Indian industries other than the remake's own (the primary frame), never later than the remake, never of its family
candidates_per_primary_pair.source: data/second/remakes/films_index.json (origin, year, family) and pairs.json (primary pairs), counted here by the rule of PLAN Section 9

candidates_per_primary_pair_source_indus.what: candidate films per primary pair, the source not counted: films of the source's industry (the scouts' frame), never later than the remake, never of its family
candidates_per_primary_pair_source_indus.source: data/second/remakes/films_index.json (origin, year, family) and pairs.json (primary pairs), counted here by the rule of PLAN Section 9

candidates_per_primary_pair_all.what: candidate films per primary pair, the source not counted: every film read, never later than the remake, never of its family
candidates_per_primary_pair_all.source: data/second/remakes/films_index.json (origin, year, family) and pairs.json (primary pairs), counted here by the rule of PLAN Section 9

pool_sizes_per_primary_pair_as_stored.what: the same sizes as the analysis stores them: they count the source, so each is one more than the candidates (PLAN Section 16, entry 6)
pool_sizes_per_primary_pair_as_stored.source: results/v2/second/remakes_words.json: counts > sets > primary > pools > <frame> > min, median, max

pair_films_that_are_documents_of_v2_refe.what: films of the kept pairs that are, in the table's older wording, documents of v2's reference corpus

primary_films_that_are_documents_of_v2_r.what: the same for the films of the primary set

primary_pairs_whose_source_is_a_referenc.what: primary pairs whose source is a document of v2's reference corpus

word_columns_of_the_word_model.what: columns of the registered word model: the designers' columns and those of the measures added by rule before the freeze

stand_ins.what: word-only stand-ins that go through the decision test in the units' place

films_asked_question_r1.what: films each model was asked question R1 about (which film is this a plot summary of?): every film of a kept pair

remakes_asked_question_r2.what: remakes each model was asked question R2 about (which earlier film does it remake?): every remake of a kept pair

statements_read_by_three_readers_that_st.what: statements read by a third reader that ended up stating a pair (the other statements read differently state none)
statements_read_by_three_readers_that_st.source: data/second/remakes/pairs.json: pairs and dropped > * > stated > * > readers equal to 3
